newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SLIP IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SLIP IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: HARARE, July 16 (Reutetr) - Zimbabwe's money market opened liquid on Wednesday with short-term trading rates quoted largely softer in sympathy, dealers said.
The market opened with an unsettled surplus of Z$22.7 million and liquidity was boosted with the maturity of Z$300 million worth of treasury bills.
Against this background the central Reserve Bank auctioned 91-day treasury bills amounting to Z$500 million at a discount rate of 24.97 percent.
Treasury bills were also being traded on the secondary market at 24.9 percent, up from 24.85 percent on Tuesday, but call money eased to 23.5 from 24 percent.

NCD bills with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted at 25.75 percent from 26.75 (buying) and were being sold a percentage point lower at 25 percent while bank acceptance bills were at 25 from 25.5 percent (buying) and were selling at 24.9 percent, slightly down from 25 percent.
